title: Stein factorization of a proper morphism to an affine scheme
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $X\xrightarrow{q}\operatorname{Spec}B\xrightarrow{s}\operatorname{Spec}A$ be its Stein factorization [def-weil-pbc-stein-factorization], $B=H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Then: (i) the ring map $A\to B$ is integral (every element of $B$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in the image of $A$); (ii) $q$ is proper; (iii) $q$ has geometrically connected fibres; in particular for every $t\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_t$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] (in particular nonempty), hence so is the subspace $q^{-1}(t)\subseteq X$, which $X_t$ maps homeomorphically onto.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Theorem 37.53.5 (Tag 03H2, label theorem-stein-factorization-general, line 15290), for $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ affine, where $S'=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(f_*\mathcal O_X)=\operatorname{Spec}H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$ (its (4)); (i) is its (2) through the affine case, (iii) is its (1) (geometrically connected with Stacks' convention that connected spaces are nonempty)

proof.text: For q = X.toSpecΓ and s = f.steinFactorizationBase, the adjunction identity q ≫ s = f is [def-weil-pbc-stein-factorization]. Since s has affine source and affine target, it is separated. Apply the exact Mathlib leaf [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated], IsProper.of_comp, to conclude that q is proper. This replaces the longer universal-factorization and finite-type cancellation argument.

The Mathlib leaf [lem-weil-pbc-stein-integral-global-sections] gives integrality of f.appTop. Precomposing with the inverse of the affine global-sections isomorphism preserves integrality (RingHom.isIntegral_respectsIso), giving the displayed map A → Γ(X, ⊤).

The canonical map q.appTop is Scheme.ΓSpecIso Γ(X, ⊤).hom and hence an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-stein-geometric-fibre-etale-criterion], it suffices to prove connectedness of each fibre after an étale base change e : U → Spec Γ(X, ⊤). Choose an affine open neighbourhood j : Spec R → U of the point t and a point v with j(v)=t. The composite e′ = j ≫ e is flat. Properness of q implies that X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-global-sections-qcqs], used through the already proved source declaration isPushout_appTop_of_flat, gives a pushout of global-section rings. Since q.appTop is invertible, the opposite pushout map p.appTop is invertible. Thus the canonical ring map R → Γ(X ×_{Spec Γ(X, ⊤)} Spec R, ⊤) is invertible. Properness of p follows by base change [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-stein-normalized-fibre-idempotent] to conclude that p.fiber v is connected and nonempty.

Pullback pasting makes the square from X × Spec R to X × U, over j : Spec R → U, Cartesian. The fibre pullback square from [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has lower map Spec of j.residueFieldMap v. An open immersion induces an isomorphism on residue fields; consequently the upper map between the two fibres is an isomorphism. Transport ConnectedSpace across its underlying homeomorphism and rewrite j(v)=t. This establishes every étale test and hence geometric connectedness of q. In Lean these are IsPullback.of_right, isPullback_fiberToSpecResidueField_of_isPullback, the open-immersion residue-field isomorphism instance, and IsPullback.isIso_fst_of_isIso.

For geometrically connected q, Mathlib supplies ConnectedSpace (q.fiber t) and Scheme.Hom.isConnected_preimage_singleton q t. The latter transports connectedness and nonemptiness through q.fiberHomeo, exactly the homeomorphism of [def-pc-scheme-fibre].
